# Findings: Unit 1.1, Fake agents, of LENDING_EXECUTION

Reviewed: 0b11a02379b3..6fa28c8dcc18, 5 files. Steps: all done.

## F1 — The implementing-role test never runs the prompt the loop builds, so it hid a real handover-path failure

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `dev/fakeagent/main_test.go:259-262`; `dev/fakeagent/act.go:35` (at 6fa28c8 it is `strings.Index`; HEAD has `strings.LastIndex`); `skills/plan-unit/SKILL.md:89`; `internal/loop/prompt.md:5-20`
- Situation: The loop fills `{{skill}}` with the `plan-unit` skill before the `## This session` block. That skill says `Write the handover to the path the prompt gives` (line 89). The test builds a hand-written prompt containing only the opening line and the `Write the handover to \`...\`` line, with no skill text.
- Happens: At 6fa28c8, `quotedAfter` took the first `Write the handover to ` and then the next backticked word, which is `DONE` in the skill's Finishing section. `implement` wrote a file named `DONE` in the repository, committed only `work.txt`, and left `DONE` untracked; the judge would fail the unit for a dirty tree. At HEAD the lookup is `LastIndex` and the fake works, but this test still passes with either lookup, so it would not catch a regression.
- Should: The test should build the prompt from `internal/loop/prompt.md` plus the `plan-unit` skill (the work order's *Start from* names `prompt.md` for where the handover path appears), assert the handover at the path the prompt names, and assert a clean tree. The extraction should read the `## This session` line, i.e. the last mention.
- Test: the existing `TestImplementingAndCollectingRoles` is the test that should show it; as written it cannot.

## F2 — A Claude weekly window at its limit reports the five-hour reset and type

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `dev/fakeagent/speak.go:62-85` (`claudeInfo`), `dev/fakeagent/scenario.go:146-153` (`spent`), `dev/fakeagent/main.go:66-74`
- Situation: `[claude]` has `session_used = 0.40`, `session_resets_in = "2h"`, `weekly_used = 1.0`, `weekly_resets_in = "96h"`; `spent` therefore returns the weekly reset for the next session.
- Happens: `speakClaudeLimit` passes the weekly reset, but `claudeInfo` derives the rejected event's `resetsAt`, `rate_limit_info.resetsAt` and `rateLimitType` from `h.Session.ResetAt` and hardcodes `five_hour`. The adapter's `rateLimit`/`Wait` uses `rate_limit_info.resetsAt` for the rejection and overrides the prose reset with it. I verified: the outcome's `RateLimit.ResetAt` was the session reset plus two minutes (`2026-10-17 16:43 +0200`) while the weekly reset was `2026-10-21 14:41 +0200`. The run retries about two hours later and hits the same weekly limit.
- Should: report the window that actually ran out: `rateLimitType: "seven_day"` and `resetsAt: unix(h.Weekly.ResetAt)` when the weekly window is the spent one, per §12 State: "A window that reaches 1 answers the next session with a usage limit until it resets."
- Test: none. `TestEachAdapterRecognisesTheSameLimit` at `dev/fakeagent/main_test.go:195` only checks that `RateLimit != nil`; add a scenario that spends the weekly window and assert `ResetAt` is around the weekly reset.

## F3 — A Codex weekly limit is reported with only a clock time, so a 96h reset is read as about 24h

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `dev/fakeagent/speak.go:184-191`; `internal/harness/harness.go` (`RateLimitFromText`, the `resetRe` parser)
- Situation: `[codex]` has `weekly_used = 1.0`, `weekly_resets_in = "96h"`; the next session takes the limit path and `spent` returns the weekly reset.
- Happens: `speakCodexLimit` writes `It resets at 12:42pm (UTC).` with no date. `RateLimitFromText` reads the next occurrence of that clock time and adds two minutes, so `Outcome.RateLimit.ResetAt` is about 24 hours away. I verified: the outcome said `2026-10-18 12:44 UTC` while the weekly window reset at `2026-10-21 14:42 UTC`. The run retries a day early and hits the limit again.
- Should: the fake's limit message must lead to the correct wait. For a weekly-spent window, omit the `resets at` clause so the Codex adapter's existing `resetOf(outcome.Budget)` fallback uses the app-server weekly reset, or name a reset the parser reads as the right instant. §12 State requires the limit to last "until it resets".
- Test: none. Add a Codex scenario that spends the weekly window and assert the outcome reset is near `Budget.Weekly.ResetAt`.

## F4 — The `red`, `dirty`, `blocked`, `nothing` and `logged-out` outcomes have no test

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `dev/fakeagent/main.go:90` (the outcome gate), `dev/fakeagent/act.go:79-90` (`dirty`/`red`), `dev/fakeagent/main_test.go:251-310` (the only role test)
- Situation: §12 lists all of these outcomes, but the tests exercise only `done` and `limit`; `TestImplementingAndCollectingRoles` uses the default `done`.
- Happens: A regression in the `outcome == "dirty"` early return, the `BROKEN` write/commit for `red`, the `act` gate at `main.go:90`, or the `logged-out` exit keeps every test green. For example, if `act` ran for `blocked`, the fake would append and commit work where the plan says it must change nothing.

This is the goal's "acts on the repository by the role of the prompt, exactly as §12 specifies", and the test guidance that every added behaviour needs a test that would fail if it broke.
- Test: none exists.

## F5 — No test covers a window whose reset has passed, or a scenario newer than the state

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `dev/fakeagent/scenario.go:132-153` (`Window.refresh`, `HarnessState.refresh`, `spent`), `dev/fakeagent/main_test.go` (whole file)

# Findings: Unit 1.2, The sandbox, of LENDING_EXECUTION

Reviewed: 6737a2d34524..583bb4144f72, 6 files. Steps: all done.

## F1 — The "last mention" lookup picks the previous handover, not the session's handover path

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `dev/fakeagent/act.go:35` and `dev/fakeagent/act.go:71`; the prompt layout is `internal/loop/prompt.md:20-27`
- Situation: The implementing prompt puts the session's own handover path on line 20, then inserts the previous unit's handover at line 27. The 1.2 handover in `docs/plans/LENDING_EXECUTION.state.json` says it took the path "from the prompt's last mention of `Write the handover to `", so it contains that marker after the session block. The same is true for any previous handover or work order that quotes the marker.
- Happens: `quotedAfter` uses `strings.LastIndex` over the whole prompt, so it starts at the later mention in the previous handover. The next backtick is the one closing that quoted marker, so it extracts the text up to the next backtick in the work order. I reproduced this with the built fake and the 1.2 handover text: `/tmp/fp/handover.md` was not written; the fake instead created an untracked file in the repository whose name is the work-order text, leaving the tree dirty.
- Should: Take the path from the `## This session` bullet (the first mention after that heading), not the last mention anywhere. §12 *Fake agents* requires the fake to write "the handover to the path the prompt names"; `internal/loop/prompt.md:20` is that path. The earlier review's "i.e. the last mention" assumed nothing after the session block repeats the phrase, which the previous-handover and work-order sections do.
- Test: Add a case to `TestImplementingAndCollectingRoles` whose prompt has a `## Handover from the previous session` section containing the phrase, and assert the session path is written and `git status --porcelain` is empty. The sandbox integration test uses the toy handovers ("Implemented unit 1.x."), so it cannot show this.

## F2 — `nix run .#sandbox -- RELATIVE_DIR` resolves the directory inside the read-only Nix store

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `flake.nix:61-64`
- Situation: `nix run .#sandbox -- ./my-sandbox`, or any relative DIR passed to the app, from the repository.
- Happens: The wrapper does `cd ${self}` (the flake source in the Nix store) before `exec go run ./dev/sandbox "$@"`. The sandbox's `filepath.Abs` therefore resolves `./my-sandbox` to `${self}/my-sandbox`, and `os.MkdirAll` fails with a read-only-filesystem or permission error. The app forwards its arguments, so it appears to accept a DIR, but a relative one can never be prepared.
- Should: Resolve DIR against the caller's working directory, as `go run ./dev/sandbox [DIR]` does. The goal says both commands set up the sandbox, and §12 step 1 says DIR is a new temp directory when not given, implying a given one works for both.
- Test: none; the flake app is not exercised by tests.

## F3 — The default scenario's values are not tested; only the three table names are

- Class: gap
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `dev/sandbox/main_test.go:55-63`; the default is `dev/sandbox/main.go:125-148`
- Situation: `defaultScenario` drops or mistypes a value, for example `[claude] session_used` becomes `session_use`, or `[codex] outcome` is removed.
- Happens: BurntSushi/toml ignores the unknown key and fakeagent defaults `outcome` to `done`. `TestPrepareBuildsTheSandbox` decodes into `map[string]any` and only checks that the `claude`, `codex` and `opencode` keys exist; `TestRunLandsTwoUnitsInTheSandbox` uses only `[opencode]`. Every test stays green although the documented default no longer exercises the windows, cost or outcomes §12 specifies.
- Should: Assert the §12 default values, or at least one representative field per table, in the layout test so a broken default is visible.
- Test: the existing `TestPrepareBuildsTheSandbox`, extended.

Reviewed: 88eeb2402b9d..c4384cbef9cd, 11 files. Steps: all done.

## F1 — The red-preflight tail is dropped when the first chosen agent cannot start

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/loop/loop.go:292-293` and `internal/loop/loop.go:841-867`
- Situation: A run starts with inherited uncommitted changes, the preflight's verify is red, and the agent `pick` chooses first is a night agent that cannot start (logged out or not installed; a `fake.Step{Err: ...}` reaches `l.benched`). The bedrock is still available.
- Happens: `l.prompt` is rendered before `l.session` starts it, and `uncommitted` clears `l.preflightRed` at `loop.go:292-293` as soon as any prompt is rendered. When `Start` returns an error the loop benches that agent and `continue`s, so the next prompt — the first prompt a session actually receives — has no `Verify is red with these changes:` block. Reproduced against c4384cb: with an inherited `inherited.txt`, a red verify and a failing night step, the night prompt carried the tail and the bedrock's first prompt did not.
- Should: Keep `preflightRed` until a session actually starts (clear it after a successful `Start`, not when a prompt is rendered), so the first session that runs carries the tail, as §3 of `LENDING.md` requires ("the failing tail of the verify log goes into the first session's prompt").
- Test: none exists. Add a loop test that combines `TestAnInheritedRedPreflightGoesToTheFirstSession` with the failing-night-step case from `TestANightAgentThatCannotRunHandsOver` and assert the primary's first prompt contains the tail.

## F2 — Resuming the same unit after a stop keeps `LeftDirty`, but no test would notice if it did not

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/loop/progress.go:67-75`, feeding the origin choice at `internal/loop/loop.go:298`
- Situation: A run is stopped mid-session, leaving `progress.Unit == "1.1"` and `progress.LeftDirty == true`; the next run resumes the same unit. §3 requires the origin sentence "An earlier attempt at this unit left these uncommitted." because `progress.forUnit(unit) && progress.LeftDirty`.
- Happens: This is the reason for the handover's `progress.reset` deviation, but nothing asserts the resumed prompt. `TestAStopMidSessionHandsItsWorkToTheNextRun` only checks the `stoppedMidUnit` failure text, and the "earlier attempt" assertion in `TestAFailedAttemptTellsTheNextOneWhy` is within one run and never exercises `reset` after the dirt exists. Reverting the `progress.go` hunk leaves `go test ./internal/loop` green (checked against c4384cb), so the behaviour can regress silently.
- Should: Assert the origin sentence on the resumed prompt, in the existing rerun-after-stop test the work order says must keep passing.
- Test: none exists; extend `TestAStopMidSessionHandsItsWorkToTheNextRun` to assert `f.h.Prompts[1]` contains `An earlier attempt at this unit left these uncommitted.` (a scratch test with that assertion passes at c4384cb and fails with the old `reset`).
